integer.summary: A whole number of platform-dependent size, written in decimal, hexadecimal, octal or binary notation.

float.summary: A double-precision floating point number, including the special values INF and NAN.

string.summary: A series of bytes; PHP strings carry no encoding and may hold arbitrary binary data.

boolean.summary: A truth value, either true or false.

singleton.summary: The unit types true, false and null, each of which has exactly one possible value.

array.summary: An ordered map of integer or string keys to values, used for lists, hash tables, stacks and queues alike.

object.summary: An instance of a class, created with new or by casting another value.

callable.summary: Anything that can be called: a function name, a closure, an object with __invoke(), or an array of object or class name and method name.

resource.summary: A handle to an external resource such as a file, a database connection or an image, created and freed by dedicated functions.

mixed.summary: Any value of any type; equivalent to the union of all other types.

void.summary: The return type of a function that returns nothing.

null.summary: The single value null, which a variable holds when it has no value.

traversable.summary: Marks a class whose instances can be iterated with foreach; it is implemented through Iterator or IteratorAggregate, never directly.

iterator.summary: Lets a class define its own iteration through the current(), key(), next(), rewind() and valid() methods.

iteratoraggregate.summary: Lets a class delegate iteration to another Traversable returned from getIterator().

arrayaccess.summary: Lets an object be accessed with array syntax through the offsetExists(), offsetGet(), offsetSet() and offsetUnset() methods.

countable.summary: Lets an object be passed to count(), which then returns the value of its count() method.

serializable.summary: Legacy interface for custom serialization through the serialize() and unserialize() methods; new code uses __serialize() and __unserialize() instead.

stringable.summary: Marks a class that defines __toString() and can therefore be converted to a string; implemented implicitly by every such class.

jsonserializable.summary: Lets an object control the data that json_encode() emits for it through the jsonSerialize() method.

throwable.summary: The base interface of everything that can be thrown, implemented by Exception and Error; user classes implement it only by extending one of those.

closure.summary: The class of every anonymous function and arrow function, also used to wrap callables and rebind their bound object and scope.

stdclass.summary: A generic empty class with dynamic properties, returned by casts to object and by functions that decode data into objects.

exception.summary: The base class of all user-level exceptions; extensions usually derive their own exception classes from it.

error.summary: The base class of all internal PHP errors that are thrown rather than reported, such as TypeError and ValueError.

typeerror.summary: Thrown when a value does not match the declared type of a parameter, property or return value, or when a function is called with too few arguments.

valueerror.summary: Thrown when an argument has the right type but an invalid value, for example an empty string where a non-empty one is required.

logicexception.summary: Represents an error in the program logic that should lead to a fix in the code; the base class of the SPL logic exceptions.

invalidargumentexception.summary: Thrown when an argument is not of the expected type or value.

outofrangeexception.summary: Thrown when an illegal index is requested and the error can be detected at compile time; the logic-error counterpart of OutOfBoundsException.

runtimeexception.summary: Thrown for errors that can only be detected while the program runs; the base class of the SPL runtime exceptions.

outofboundsexception.summary: Thrown when a value is not a valid key, where this cannot be detected before the code runs.

underflowexception.summary: Thrown when an invalid operation is performed on an empty container, such as removing an element from an empty list.

unexpectedvalueexception.summary: Thrown when a value does not match a set of expected values, typically when a function returns something it should not.

INI_USER.summary: The ini directive can be set in user scripts and in the Windows registry.

INI_PERDIR.summary: The ini directive can be set in php.ini, .htaccess, httpd.conf and .user.ini.

INI_SYSTEM.summary: The ini directive can only be set in php.ini or httpd.conf.

INI_ALL.summary: The ini directive can be set anywhere.

E_ERROR.summary: Fatal run-time error that halts the script.

E_WARNING.summary: Run-time warning that does not halt the script.

E_NOTICE.summary: Run-time notice about something that might be an error but might also occur during normal execution.

E_USER_WARNING.summary: User-generated warning message raised with trigger_error().

PHP_VERSION.summary: The current PHP version as a string, for example "8.5.0".

PHP_ZTS.summary: Whether PHP was built with thread safety enabled.

PHP_INT_MAX.summary: The largest integer supported on this build of PHP.

PHP_INT_MIN.summary: The smallest integer supported on this build of PHP.

PHP_INT_SIZE.summary: The size of an integer in bytes on this build of PHP.

STDIN.summary: An already opened stream to standard input, available in the CLI SAPI.

INF.summary: The floating point value for infinity.

SEEK_SET.summary: Set the stream position to the given offset from the start of the stream.

SEEK_CUR.summary: Set the stream position to the current position plus the given offset.

SEEK_END.summary: Set the stream position to the end of the stream plus the given offset.

LC_CTYPE.summary: Locale category for character classification and conversion, such as strtoupper().

SIGHUP.summary: Signal sent when the controlling terminal is closed.

SIGINT.summary: Interrupt signal, typically sent by pressing Ctrl+C.

SIGALRM.summary: Signal sent when a timer set with alarm() expires.

SIGCHLD.summary: Signal sent to a parent process when a child process stops or terminates.

SIGIO.summary: Signal sent when asynchronous I/O is possible on a descriptor.

CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER.summary: Whether cURL verifies the peer's TLS certificate.

CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYHOST.summary: How strictly cURL checks that the TLS certificate matches the host name.

CURLOPT_RESOLVE.summary: An array of host:port:address strings that override DNS resolution for the transfer.
